  Readable gloss: "Eder is a masculine noun for a flock or herd of domestic animals, appearing 38 times from Genesis through Malachi. It enters Scripture at the well where Jacob meets Rachel: 'three flocks of sheep were lying beside it' (Gen 29:2). The word's pastoral warmth is distilled in Isaiah 40:11, where the Lord 'will tend his flock like a shepherd.' Yet eder also carries economic weight — it represents wealth (Gen 32:17; 2 Chr 32:28) and covenantal obligation (Mal 1:14, condemning those who vow from the flock but sacrifice a blemished animal). The prophets use flocks as a figure for desolation: Isaiah envisions abandoned cities where 'flocks shall lie down' (Isa 17:2; 32:14). Song of Songs draws on the pastoral image differently, comparing the beloved's hair to 'a flock of goats descending from Gilead' (4:1; 6:6)."

Frequently appears in construct: eder tso'n ('flock of sheep,' Gen 29:2; Joel 1:18), eder hare...
